original_forecast.resolution_rule: Resolve against the first Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI release for July 2026. Event succeeds if the reported all-items CPI 12-month percent change is less than or equal to 3.4%. Do not use later revisions for the initial score.
rationale: Pre-release coverage centers on 3.4% year-over-year headline CPI after 3.5% in June, so the threshold is deliberately close to consensus rather than an extreme tail.
June inflation cooled sharply as energy retreated, but renewed July/August geopolitical oil pressure creates upside risk and prevents a high-confidence disinflation forecast.
This event directly discriminates the H001 disinflation path from the H003 inflation-regime risk more cleanly than one additional equity close.
surprising_if: Headline CPI prints 3.6% or higher despite the prior-month disinflation evidence.
Headline CPI prints 3.2% or lower despite renewed energy/geopolitical pressure.

resolution.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics first July 2026 CPI release, 2026-08-12 08:30 ET.
resolution.audit_note: Forecast content above is preserved verbatim. The event resolved true at exactly 3.4% YoY. The proper score is favorable, but the forecast threshold equaled the published consensus point and the outcome exactly matched that consensus; therefore this result is not evidence of informational skill versus consensus. It was scored before the CPI details or subsequent market reaction were used for model revision.
